title: Vitest 10-second gate collapses under sustained multi-agent host CPU saturation
outcome: The UI gate has a fixed 10-second per-test diagnostic budget and maxWorkers=2, but on 2026-07-31 the host was saturated by a Virtualization VM at about 88% CPU, Docker, and many long-lived agent processes. Full Vitest took 889.97s and reached 2593/2615 before one timeout caused overlapping-act cascades across preferences, visibility, workspace-layout, and DnD. A single-file App.preferences diagnostic reproduced the timeout: first heavy test 10.78s, transform 69.45s, import 111.40s, with Vitest receiving about 12% CPU. The vite.config comment refers to tm-g4z, but that ID is absent from the current Beads DB. Do not solve by increasing timeouts or retries. Add a deterministic resource preflight or runner isolation/CPU reservation so the unchanged 10-second budget remains meaningful under supported multi-agent operation.
acceptance: A full 2615-test Vitest gate and the isolated App.preferences suite pass without retries, sleeps, quarantine, or increased timeouts while the supported TermAl multi-agent workload is active; when host resources are insufficient, the gate fails fast before running tests with an explicit resource diagnostic instead of cascading React act failures.
